scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to let my 7-year-old brother stay up late instead of going to bed. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that my brother is pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough, he gets all out of sorts the next day. That makes sense because kids his age need a lot of sleep to function properly. I remember when I was younger, I used to get really cranky if I didn't get enough sleep too. Last night, my mom left me in charge and trusted me to have my friend over. I made sure my brother went to bed on time because he can put himself to bed. But then my friend came over, and we started goofing around, watching a movie, and being a bit loud. My brother woke up and came downstairs, wanting to watch the movie with us. I told him to go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. I was in a tough spot. If I tried to force him to go to bed, I knew he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing and exhausting. Plus, my friend was there, and I didn't want to cause a scene. So I let him stay, and by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home, my brother was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him in bed. It was midnight, which is way later than his usual bedtime. The next morning, he didn't want to get up, even though on weekends he's not allowed to sleep past 8. He was pretty cranky. My mom found out and got mad at me. She knows I let him stay up late. I told her that since he's 7, he should know about consequences and that if he stays up later, he won't feel good. I also mentioned that two hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by not forcing him to go to bed. On one hand, I didn't want to deal with the tantrum and the embarrassment in front of my friend. On the other hand, I know that getting enough sleep is important for him, and maybe I should have been firmer about it. I think about what my mom said. She trusts me to take care of my brother, but in this case, she was upset because I didn't enforce the bedtime. I can see her perspective because she knows how important sleep is for him. But I also thought that two hours wasn't a huge deal, especially since he was able to fall asleep on the couch and I carried him up. I also consider my brother's feelings. He was excited to watch the movie with us, and my friend was hyping him up. I didn't want to make him feel bad or excluded. But by letting him stay up, I knew he would be cranky the next day, which would make things harder for everyone, including me. Maybe I should have found a middle ground. Like, let him watch part of the movie but then gently insist he go to bed. Or maybe set a timer so he knows when it's time to go. That way, he wouldn't feel excluded, but he also wouldn't stay up too late. I also think about the consequences. If I let him stay up late this time, does that set a precedent for future times? He might expect to stay up every time my friend comes over, which could lead to more arguments and more crankiness the next day. In the end, I understand why my mom was upset. She values my brother's well-being and routine, and she trusts me to uphold that. Even though I thought two hours wasn't a big deal, it's probably better to stick to the routine to ensure he gets enough sleep consistently. So, maybe I should have been firmer about enforcing bedtime, even if it meant dealing with a tantrum. It's better for his health and well-being in the long run, and it sets a good example for him about the importance of sleep and routines.
